text:
devrel: Heads-up: we're running an Open Source Plugins Sprint next Tue (May 6). Goal: showcase community-built plugins that extend Redwood (connectors, evals, runtime adapters, monitoring hooks). Call for demos: 90s video + PR link. Submit here: https://forms.redwood.ai/os-plugins-sprint (deadline May 2). We'll highlight winners at Community Day and give maintainers a "community maintainer" badge + swag. :tada:

maya: Nice! Any guidance on the 90s video? Prefer screencast or talking head?

devrel: No strict format. Prefer concise demos showing 1) what it does, 2) how to run locally, 3) a quick example output. Screencast with captions works well. We added a tiny demo script in the community-templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-templates/blob/main/demo-script.md :sparkles:

sam: License Q: my plugin reuses a tiny snippet from a BSD-licensed lib. Is that okay?

alice: We prefer MIT/Apache-2.0 for submitted plugins. BSD is generally compatible but please include the upstream copyright and a LICENSE file in your repo and note attribution in the PR body. If it's borderline, loop in @legal-team.

release-bot: Reminder: submissions before May 1 get early review. Priority feedback window closes in 48h. Submit via: https://forms.redwood.ai/os-plugins-sprint

devrel: Quick PR checklist (paste into your PR body):

```
- README with one-line description + quickstart (how to run locally)
- LICENSE (MIT or Apache-2.0 preferred)
- minimal test or quick smoke script (e.g., `python examples/run_demo.py`)
- link to 90s demo video (YouTube/Streamable)
```

maya: How are demos judged? Will there be a rubric?

devrel: Yes, we'll score on: novelty, integration quality (does it follow the connectors/adapters contract), reproducibility (can we run it in 10 min), and docs. Judges: DevRel + 2 community maintainers + 1 eng reviewer.

sam: Can I demo a runtime adapter that changes KV-cache behaviour? It touches internal cache keys but not user data.

devrel: That's fine for the sprint, but if it inspects runtime customer payloads we need a security review before we feature it publicly. If it's purely performance/adapter logic, good to go.

alice: Also remind folks to avoid embedding any customer data in demo recordings. If your demo uses sample data, mark it as synthetic. CC @legal-team for license questions.

devrel: We'll host an office hours review session this Thurs 16:00 PT (30m slots). RSVP: https://calendar.redwood.ai/os-plugins-office-hours. DM me if you want a pre-review slot. Looking forward to the builds! :rocket:
